problem: LM-based VLN-CE agents (e.g., NaVid) assume clean visual input and lose up to about half their success rate under real-world corruptions such as noise, fog and snow. Existing blind denoisers, test-time adaptation and diffusion-based decorruptors process frames independently, ignore temporal and action consistency, and are slow.
motivation: Real robots face motion blur, lighting changes, weather and sensor noise, which distort cues needed for action prediction. Retraining the large frozen backbone is costly and risks forgetting, and iterative diffusion is too slow for online navigation. Since LM agents infer ego-motion from image histories, inter-frame consistency matters more than per-frame visual quality.
key_idea: A plug-in latent conditional flow matching decorruptor conditioned on previous-frame information and atomic actions, with action-centroid Mahalanobis filtering that decides when to fuse temporally conditioned outputs.
insight: Temporal consistency, not per-frame realism, drives navigation gains. FlowDec beats Dec-DPM and Dec-CM, which are distilled from a 45M-pair model, despite training only on R2R-CE/RxR-CE, and it has the lowest warp error. Ablations show that training with the temporal conditions improves even c1-only inference, that starting from a partly corrupted latent (t_theta=0.95) helps, and that fewer Euler steps (5-10) cost little.
method: Latent CFM decorruptor: a U-Net velocity field in VAE latent space is trained with a constant-velocity linear-path flow matching loss to map noise to the clean latent, conditioned on the corrupted latent.

Hybrid temporal conditions: c1 uses the current augmented latent only. c2 adds the previous frame's (augmented minus GT) latent and the previous action. c3 adds the previous (augmented minus denoised) latent and the action. Training weights are c1=0.3 fixed, with c2 gradually replaced by c3 over epochs. Corruptions are simulated with PixMix+SimSiam augmentation.

Action centroids: per atomic action (forward 25cm, turn L/R 15°/30°), a diagonal Gaussian is fit to differential latents of consecutive GT frames, using 2.44M image pairs from R2R-CE/RxR-CE train splits.

Action-centroid guided filtering: c1 is the primary output. The mean Mahalanobis distance w between the previous and current decorrupted latents and the action centroid is computed. If w>0.25, c3 is also run and the two outputs are fused with weights inversely proportional to distance when w~<w.
Shortened flow start: integration starts from z0'=t_theta*noise+(1-t_theta)*corrupted latent with t_theta=0.95, using a 20-step Euler solver, which speeds up inference and reduces randomness.
Model-agnostic plug-in: the module is placed in front of a frozen VLN agent (NaVid, Uni-NaVid) and uses the agent's predicted actions, with no retraining of the backbone.

setting.backbone: NaVid (Vicuna-7B + EVA-CLIP, frozen) with a FlowDec latent CFM U-Net + VAE trained as a front-end; Uni-NaVid in the appendix
setting.training_data: FlowDec is trained only on RGB image pairs collected from R2R-CE and RxR-CE training episodes in Habitat (~2.44M pairs, 5 atomic actions) with synthetic PixMix+SimSiam corruption. The navigation backbone is unchanged.
setting.observation: monocular RGB video stream (corrupted) plus instruction
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 25cm / TURN 15° or 30° / STOP, parsed from LLM text
setting.simulator: Habitat (R2R-CE, RxR-CE with synthetic corruptions) plus real-world Unitree GO2
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT frames are used only in training for centroids and c2)

numbers_note: Split names are not stated explicitly. The 1,839 and 3,669 episode counts match the val-unseen sets, so this is an assumption. Per-corruption numbers are in the tables but only averages are listed here. Real-robot results are success rates over 20 trials per task, and are not benchmark entries (NaVid vs FlowDec: Task1 0.20 vs 0.35, Task2 0.05 vs 0.20, Task3 0.10 vs 0.30, Task4 0.35 vs 0.40). Inference time: 370ms for NaVid plus 173ms for FlowDec (text says 169 ms).
results: Averaged over six corruptions, FlowDec raises NaVid from 21.58 to 27.04 SR on R2R-CE and from 30.75 to 33.63 SR on RxR-CE, beating Dec-DPM, Dec-CM (24.29/29.12) and SCUNet. It has the lowest average warp error (0.11/0.13) and decorrupts 3-8x faster than the diffusion baselines. It is nearly lossless on clean input and improves real-robot success on all four tasks.
limitations: Evaluated mainly with synthetic corruptions, on NaVid (plus Uni-NaVid in the appendix), and with a small real-robot test (20 trials per task).
Slightly lower performance on clean inputs and on some corruptions (Snow on R2R-CE, JPEG SPL on RxR-CE); it adds 173 ms of overhead per step.
It relies on the agent's predicted atomic actions and on centroids fitted from simulator data, and handles only static rather than dynamically varying noise.
